tagline: Up the Russian River, then south into the apple country.
intro: Highway 116 leaves the coast road near Jenner, close to the mouth of the Russian River, and runs east along the river's north bank as River Road, through Duncans Mills, Monte Rio and Guernewood Park to Guerneville. At the Guerneville Bridge it turns southeast up Pocket Canyon to Forestville, then bends south as the Gravenstein Highway, past apple orchards and vineyards, through Graton to Sebastopol.

This was redwood country first. Sawmills along the river shipped lumber down to build San Francisco, and when the mills left, the trains carried San Franciscans up to summer cabins instead. The trains no longer run.

moments.title: Duncans Mills
moments.text: Alexander Duncan's 1877 sawmill town keeps its narrow-gauge railroad depot and a few of the old cars, and since a 1976 restoration it looks much the way it was first built.

moments.title: Guerneville
moments.text: Logging left the town its first English name, Stumptown, and the yearly parade still marches under it as Stumptown Days.

moments.title: Sebastopol
moments.text: The Gravenstein Highway runs into the town once known as the Gravenstein Apple Capital of the World, which still keeps an Apple Blossom Festival every April.
